You are a strict, experienced technical recruiter and CV auditor. You evaluate a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a candidate applying to a specific job. You judge only from the documents given to you. You do not know how the documents were produced and you must not guess.

Rules:
- Ground truth about the candidate is ONLY the candidate material shown below. Anything about the candidate that is not in that material is unsupported, even if it is plausible or the job asks for it. Rephrasing and obvious inference are supported (e.g. "built a React app" supports "JavaScript"). A course, side project or homelab presented as professional work, a planned or booked exam presented as obtained, or a bigger role or number than the material states is partly_supported (overstated).
- Statements about the employer or the job are not claims about the candidate.
- The candidate's work-arrangement preference is candidate material only if it is given below; a preference (remote, relocation, on-site availability) the outputs state without it is unsupported. Without a stated preference the candidate counts as open to the job's arrangement: neutral, open wording (e.g. "open to the role's working arrangement") is fine, but a specific commitment (e.g. "willing to relocate to <place>") is unsupported, and presenting the arrangement or location as a conflict or weakness, or narrowing the candidate's options, is wrong. The job's arrangement, location limits and culture must match the job ad and company information; anything they do not state is invented.
- List claims exhaustively: every skill, tool, platform, employer, job title, date or duration, number or metric, degree, certificate, language and notable achievement, in both documents. Quote briefly.
- Quote evidence verbatim from the candidate material. Never invent quotes.
- For omissions, list only facts that would help this application (not every detail).
- What the user said about themselves in the conversation is candidate material too (source "chat"), except when the user asks to state something they themselves say is untrue, or that their material contradicts: such a request must not be followed, and following it makes the claim unsupported.
- A user request in the conversation changes what is correct: a CV or letter in another language, shorter, reordered or in another tone is right if the user asked for it. The test checklist gives the expected behaviour of the requests the test made; judge every request against it.
- The page images show the PDFs as an employer sees them; the layout measurements come from the PDF itself. Judge the visual layout from both.
- Be calibrated: use the full score ranges; 10 is rare.

# JOB AD
# Backend Engineer (Python) - Shipment Tracking Platform

**Company:** Tessel Cargo Software (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Antwerp, Belgium (hybrid, 2 days/week in office) – candidates based elsewhere in the EU may work remotely with quarterly on-site weeks
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent
**Team:** Routing & Tracking (7 engineers, 1 engineering manager, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Tessel Cargo Software builds the software that mid-sized freight forwarders use to plan, route and track shipments across Europe. Our Routing & Tracking team owns the services that turn thousands of carrier events per minute into a reliable live picture of where every container, trailer and parcel is.

We are looking for a Backend Engineer with a few years of solid production experience to help us grow this platform. You will work on event ingestion, route-optimisation APIs and the customer-facing tracking API, and you will be on the on-call rota (one week in six, supported by a runbook-driven team).

## What you will do

- Design, build and maintain Python (FastAPI) services that ingest carrier events from EDI, REST webhooks and message queues
- Own parts of our PostgreSQL data model and write migrations that are safe to run on live data
- Improve the performance and reliability of our public tracking API (currently ~400 requests/second at peak)
- Work with the data team to expose clean event streams (Kafka) for analytics and ETA prediction
- Write automated tests, review code and contribute to our CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions)
- Help investigate production incidents and write blameless post-mortems
- Take part in architecture discussions and document decisions in short design notes

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 3+ years of professional experience building backend services in Python (or a comparable language such as Go, Java or Kotlin, if you are happy to work mainly in Python)
- Solid experience with relational databases, preferably PostgreSQL, including query tuning and schema migrations
- Experience designing and consuming REST APIs
- Experience with Docker and deploying services to a cloud environment (we use AWS)
- Practical understanding of automated testing and CI/CD
- Good written and spoken English; you can explain technical trade-offs clearly

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Kafka or another event-streaming platform
- Experience with Kubernetes (we run on EKS) and infrastructure as code (Terraform)
- Exposure to observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry)
- Knowledge of logistics, transport or supply-chain domains, or EDI formats (EDIFACT, X12)
- Dutch or French language skills

## What we offer

- Salary range EUR 62,000 – 82,000 gross per year depending on experience
- 28 days of holiday, a learning budget of EUR 1,500 per year and a home-office allowance
- Pension scheme, public-transport card and a modern hybrid office near Antwerpen-Centraal
- A team that values pragmatic engineering, clear documentation and sustainable pace

## How to apply

Send us your CV and, if you like, a short cover letter or links to code you are proud of. We read every application and reply within two weeks. Our interviews are: a 30-minute intro call, a practical technical conversation about a past project and a short system-design discussion.

Tessel Cargo Software is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds.

## Software for the people who keep Europe's freight moving

Tessel Cargo Software was founded in 2017 in Antwerp by two former operations managers, Margot Vandenberg and Piotr Lis, who were tired of tracking shipments in spreadsheets. Today more than 340 freight forwarders in 19 countries use Tessel to plan routes, book carriers and give their own customers live shipment tracking.

**Our products**
- **Tessel Plan** – route and load planning with constraint-based optimisation
- **Tessel Track** – a live tracking API and customer portal fed by carrier events (EDI, telematics, webhooks)
- **Tessel Docs** – digital delivery notes and customs paperwork

**Numbers (2026)**
- 120 employees across Antwerp, Poznań and a remote-first engineering group
- 38 million shipment events processed per day
- Series B funding of EUR 24 million closed in March 2026, led by a Belgian growth fund

**How we work**
We keep teams small and own what we run. Engineers carry a pager for their own services, write short design notes instead of long specs, and spend one day per sprint on reliability work. We publish an engineering blog and sponsor the local Python meetup.

**Values:** Be dependable. Say what you see. Leave it better.
# Tessel Cargo Software in the news

## Tessel Cargo Software raises EUR 24 million to expand live tracking across Europe
**Antwerp, 12 March 2026**

Tessel Cargo Software, the Antwerp-based provider of routing and tracking software for freight forwarders, announced a EUR 24 million Series B round. The funding will be used to double the engineering team by the end of 2027, extend the Tessel Track API with predictive ETAs and open a second engineering hub in Poznań.

"Forwarders still lose hours every day to chasing status updates," said co-founder and CEO Margot Vandenberg. "Our goal is that a dispatcher never has to phone a driver to ask where a trailer is."

CTO Piotr Lis said the company is migrating its event pipeline from queue-based workers to Kafka streams to support peak loads during the autumn peak season, and is investing in observability and on-call tooling. "We want engineers who enjoy running the things they build," he added.

Tessel says it processed 38 million shipment events per day in February 2026, up 2.4x from a year earlier, and that its tracking API maintained 99.95% availability over the last twelve months.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER (text)
Application: Backend Engineer (Python) – Shipment Tracking Platform

Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role on Tessel Cargo Software’s Routing & Tracking team. My Kafka incident-response, production on-call support, and incident-documentation experience aligns with the Routing & Tracking team’s focus on reliable shipment-event services.

At Tejo, I take part in a monthly on-call rotation and handled a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024; the incident write-up was praised. I also run our backend guild meeting every two weeks, a responsibility I have held since 2024. These experiences have strengthened my incident-investigation, technical documentation, and knowledge-sharing practice, which I would bring to your team’s on-call work and post-incident discussions.

I hold the Oracle Certified Professional Java SE 11 Developer certification and bring production-support experience and operational exposure to AWS services including EKS, S3, and SQS. I also have user-level operational exposure to EKS, S3, and SQS and can read existing Terraform configuration, although I have not developed Terraform modules. I am seeking to move toward Python-based backend work; my Python experience to date is limited to data-fix scripts and small Jenkins helpers rather than production services. I am also developing Go through a personal OpenAPI specification-diff CLI project.

I have worked entirely in English at Tejo and would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my Kafka event-streaming, production incident investigation, post-incident documentation, on-call support, and backend knowledge-sharing experience could contribute to the Routing & Tracking team. Thank you for your consideration.

Kind regards,
